name: Citizenship by Registration (Marriage)

requirements.blocker_text: Married to a Kenyan citizen (marriage solemnized under Kenyan law, in Kenya or abroad) for at least 7 years, with the marriage subsisting at the time of application.
requirements.fix_path: Remain validly married to the Kenyan citizen spouse for 7 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Must have acquired residence status in Kenya.
Must not be a declared prohibited immigrant or have been convicted of an offence carrying a sentence of 3 years or more.
Marriage must not have been entered into for the purpose of acquiring an immigration or citizenship status or privilege.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate (Kenyan law-compliant, in Kenya or abroad)
Evidence the marriage is genuine and subsisting

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 7 years of marriage plus acquired residence status

sources.title: Kenya Law (official government legal database) -- Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Act 2011, Section 11: registration for a person married to a Kenyan citizen requires the marriage to have subsisted at least 7 years, acquired residence status, no prohibited-immigrant declaration or 3+ year criminal conviction, a genuine (non-immigration-motivated) marriage still subsisting at application

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kenya). Published on tier-1 sourcing (Kenya Law, the government's own legal database). GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING, CONSISTENT WITH ke_citizenship_by_descent.json: Section 11 is gender-neutral on its face ('a person married to a Kenyan citizen'), unlike the many one-directional gendered marriage-citizenship provisions found elsewhere in this dataset (Qatar, Bahrain, Nigeria, Sudan, Somalia, Pakistan). The 7-year marriage-plus-residence requirement is long by comparative standards in this dataset (contrast e.g. Sudan's 2-year fast-track, gendered as it is), reflecting a generally more demanding standard across all of Kenya's registration/naturalisation routes (see ke_citizenship_naturalisation.json's matching 7-year figure). dual_citizenship_allowed TRUE, per Kenya's 2010 Constitution and this Act's general dual-citizenship allowance (see ke_citizenship_by_descent.json notes).
